content: ZZZ3, also known as ZZ-type zinc finger-containing protein 3, is a protein encoded by the ZZZ3 gene in humans. To investigate the function of ZZZ3, model organisms have been utilized. Specifically, a conditional knockout mouse line, named Zzz3tm1a(EUCOMM)Wtsi, was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a large-scale mutagenesis initiative aimed at generating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers worldwide. Both male and female mice from this knockout line underwent a standardized series of phenotypic tests to assess the consequences of ZZZ3 gene deletion. A total of 24 different tests were conducted on the mutant mice. Among these, two significant abnormalities were identified. Notably, no homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation, indicating that embryos with two copies of the mutated gene failed to survive to the weaning stage. As a result, the remaining tests were performed on heterozygous mutant adult mice, which carry only one copy of the mutated gene. In these heterozygous mice, no additional abnormal phenotypes were observed.
